r.정치 구도: The president is a ceremonial head of state chosen by parliament, and the leader of the largest party in the 300-seat parliament becomes prime minister and runs the government. After the debt crisis broke out in 2010, Greece took three bailouts from the European Union and the International Monetary Fund and endured years of austerity that cut pensions and wages. The old two-party system collapsed along the way, and the radical-left Syriza even held power for a time. Since 2019 the center-right New Democracy has governed alone, and it won the 2023 election by a wide margin. Large protests every year over the 2023 Tempi train collision, which killed 57 people, and an investigation into farm subsidy fraud keep up the pressure on the government. The next election must be held by 2027.

t.why: Greek shipowners are counted as the group that controls the largest merchant fleet in the world. That is why Greece keeps coming up in shipping news, from the price cap on Russian oil to threats against Red Sea routes. It has long quarreled with Turkey over maritime boundaries and airspace around the Aegean islands, a dispute tied up with the division of Cyprus in 1974. It is often the first place migrants from the Middle East and Africa reach in Europe, which puts it on the front line of EU asylum policy. It joined NATO in 1952 and the European Community, forerunner of the EU, in 1981. During the debt crisis there was open talk of it leaving the euro, and it stood at the center of the eurozone crisis.
t.rel: It has a long-running dispute with Turkey over Aegean islands and sea boundaries. Because northern Greece also has a region called Macedonia, Greece objected for nearly 30 years to its neighbor using the same name and blocked its entry into NATO and the EU. The dispute ended when the neighbor renamed itself North Macedonia in 2019, and North Macedonia joined NATO the following year.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations began in 1961. Greece fought in the Korean War, sending an army battalion and an air force transport flight. Shipbuilding is the strongest economic tie. Greek owners have long been major customers of Korean shipyards, and in the first half of 2025 Korean yards won close to 65% of new ships ordered by Greek owners. Orders shifted further toward Korea after the United States moved to charge port fees on Chinese-built ships. At a July 2026 meeting of foreign ministers, the two sides also discussed Korean shipbuilders taking part in modernizing the Greek navy.
t.know: Its national anthem comes from a 158-verse poem, making its lyrics the longest of any anthem.
etext: Ships owned by Greek shipowners make up the world's largest fleet by carrying capacity. Most fly other countries' flags and earn their money at sea, but ship finance, insurance and jobs for seafarers bring that money home.

Every year more than three times the country's population comes to visit its islands and ruins, making tourism a pillar of the economy. Visitors crowd into the summer, so jobs and income swing heavily with the seasons.

After leaving its bailout program in 2018, Greece ran budget surpluses and paid down debt, and in 2023 its credit rating returned to investment grade. Its debt ratio is still the highest in the EU, but it is also falling faster than anywhere else.

Many young, skilled people left during the crisis, and the population is shrinking and aging. Manufacturing is weak and small family businesses dominate, so productivity is low. Wages lag far behind the European average while rents and prices have risen, fueling discontent.
